## What The Quiz Measures

Quiz 2 asks you to connect a MATLAB result to the evidence needed to trust or
interpret it. It is more challenging than Quiz 1 because several questions
require a conceptual decision, but it does not depend on obscure syntax or
speed. You will not be asked to write a long program from a blank page.

The six content blocks sample these ideas:

- arrays, logical indexing, `end`, and row/column orientation;
- functions, explicit inputs, workspace scope, and clean-run reliability;
- polynomial fitting, residuals, fit/check RMSE, and overfitting evidence;
- root finding, substituted residuals, numerical integration, and refinement
  checks;
- symbolic exactness, assumptions, and admissible solutions;
- stationary points and the additional evidence needed to support a minimum.

Some questions share a short code fragment or evidence display, but each
question is scored separately. The two sections receive equivalent forms that
use substantially different representations and solution routes, rather than
the same questions with changed numerical values.

## Practice Quiz

An ungraded practice quiz will be available in Blackboard. It has the same
12-question rhythm and approximate first-attempt duration, but it does not
reproduce either live form. Every practice block asks you to audit a plausible
AI or student claim, identify missing evidence, or choose a stronger check.

Use the first attempt as a 15-minute simulation without MATLAB or AI. The
practice activity allows repeated attempts and self-check feedback; its score
does not contribute to the course grade. The purpose is to practice the
reasoning standard, not to memorize a template for the live quiz.

## Rules During The Quiz

Quiz 2 is individual. You may bring **one A4 sheet, handwritten by you, using
both sides**. Printed material and additional reference sheets are not allowed.
Do not use MATLAB, AI tools, websites, messaging, another student, or other
electronic resources. Blank scratch paper is allowed. Use the classroom
computer unless the instructor announces another arrangement.

If Blackboard is unavailable, the instructor may use an equivalent paper
version. Approved accommodations follow the usual course arrangements.

A student arriving after the quiz has begun may take it only while it remains
available; the common closing time is not extended because of late arrival. A
missed quiz follows the [syllabus policy on missed
assessments](../syllabus/index.qmd#missed-assessments-and-late-project-submissions).

## How To Prepare

1. Review the survival checklists and core examples for [Week
   1](../weeks/week-01.qmd), [Week 2](../weeks/week-02.qmd), [Week
   3](../weeks/week-03.qmd), [Week 4](../weeks/week-04.qmd), and [Week
   5](../weeks/week-05.qmd).
2. For each calculation, practice answering two questions: “What did MATLAB
   compute?” and “What does this result establish—and what does it not
   establish?”
3. Practice one-sentence explanations of a hidden input, poor check-set
   performance, and a valid minimum check.
4. Use the handwritten sheet to organize concepts and validation patterns;
   copying long scripts is less useful than recording what each check means.

For written responses, state the essential reason directly. Mathematically
correct equivalent wording is accepted; polished or extended writing is not
required. The actual questions and answers are not published on this site.
